findings.title: Shipped evaluation code cannot consume the logs of most reported experiments
findings.quote:
- We share logs of most of our experiments under `logs`.
- Please note that some logs were generated with our previous code base and the logs were saved in a slightly different scheme. Please refer to `old_code` branch (we will add more details TBD).
findings.claim: The only evaluation entrypoints (evaluate_deals.ipynb, score_leakage.py) select logs with filename.startswith('history') and call eval_utils.load_setup(), which opens config.txt and scores_files/ inside the log dir (eval_utils.py:7-8). But all 23 zipped archives in logs/ are old-format: answers*.json / full_conversation*.json with list-valued 'rounds' and no config.txt or scores_files/ (verified via `unzip -l` + JSON inspection); README Logs section (quoted) admits these came from a 'previous code base' and defers the compatible parser to an absent 'old_code' branch.
findings.concern: Most headline numbers cannot be recomputed from the repo as shipped, including the primary base-game GPT-4 result (Table 1 row 5 / Table 3 / Table 8 temp=0: 81/33/100/1.4), all of Table 3's per-model rows, Table 2 (mixed population), Table 4's Base/rewrite/new-games/difficulty rows, Table 6 variants, and Table 9 — contradicting checklist 3(a) ('code needed to reproduce the main experimental results [Yes]'); only the two new-format logs (7-player extended and temp=1) are runnable, and those I reproduced (see check script).
findings.resolution: Please add the 'old_code' evaluation parser (or convert the shared answers*.json logs, plus their config.txt/scores_files, into the current history* schema) so the main-table numbers can be recomputed end-to-end.

findings.title: Heuristic rule-based baseline (Table 5) has no implementation in the repo
findings.quote: we start with a random deal and select one agent at a time to improve over the last proposed deal by changing one option at a time until its corresponding minimum threshold is met or no more changes can be made
findings.claim: Table 5 reports 5/6-way and 6-way success for a repeated rule-based (LLM-free) baseline over base and new games; the described procedure (greedy per-issue improvement over randomized starts/orders) is a concrete algorithm.
findings.concern: No script in the repo implements this baseline (grep over all .py/.ipynb finds no such routine, and there is no baseline log), so the Table 5 numbers cannot be reproduced or checked.
findings.resolution: Please add the rule-based baseline generator used for Table 5, or the deals it produced.

findings.title: ToM 'best guess' preference-matching experiment (61% / 42%) has no code or ground truth
findings.quote: GPT-4 models scored 61% in correctly matching the ground truth preferences of sub-options, vs. 42% by GPT-3.5
findings.claim: Section 4.2 reports a headline capability result: agents are separately prompted to guess each party's preferred sub-option per issue and scored against ground-truth preferences.
findings.concern: The repo contains no preference-elicitation prompt/driver, no ground-truth preference labels, and no scoring script for this experiment, so 61%/42% cannot be traced or reproduced.
findings.resolution: Please add the preference-elicitation prompt, the ground-truth sub-option preference file, and the matching/scoring script.

findings.title: Prompt-structure ablation (Table 1) not reproducible: scratchpad is fixed, no toggles
findings.claim: The round prompt's scratchpad is chosen solely by incentive and each *_scratch_pad() returns a single hardcoded string; the CLI (main.py) exposes no switches to remove the five ablated CoT components (previous-deal calculation, inferring others' preferences, candidate generation, selection, planning).
findings.concern: Table 1 systematically ablates five prompt components across 12 rows (the paper's core 'prompt structure matters' result), but the code ships only the final prompt per incentive and there are no per-row logs, so none of the ablation rows except the 'best' one can be regenerated.
findings.resolution: Please add the prompt variants (or flags) used to produce each Table 1 row, or the logs for the ablated configurations.

findings.title: Interactive random-deal baseline (10%/3%) has no incentive/mode in the code
findings.quote: We add a baseline where we prompt GPT-4 agents to give a random deal at each round
findings.claim: Section 4.7 reports final success 10%/3% (5/6-way) over 120 sessions for a variant where agents propose random deals each round.
findings.concern: rounds.py / initial_prompts.py support only cooperative, greedy, untargeted_adv, targeted_adv incentives; there is no 'random' proposal mode and no log for it, so this baseline is not reproducible.
findings.resolution: Please add the random-deal prompting mode (or its logs) used for this baseline.

findings.title: Non-Azure OpenAI path returns the Message object, not its .content string
findings.quote:
if 'gpt' in self.model and not self.azure:        
            messages = self.messages + [ {"role": role, "content": msg} ]
            response = self.client.chat.completions.create(model=self.model, messages=messages,temperature=self.temperature)
            content = response.choices[0].message
            return content
findings.claim: In the non-Azure OpenAI branch, prompt() returns response.choices[0].message (a ChatCompletionMessage object); every other branch (Azure, Gemini, HF) returns a string (the Azure branch on line 69 returns response.choices[0].message.content).
findings.concern: The returned value flows to save_conversation -> process_answer -> extract_answer, which calls answer.split('<ANSWER>') and json.dump; a Message object has no .split and is not JSON-serializable, so the documented OpenAI-API (non-Azure) run path crashes — .content is missing on this branch only.
findings.resolution: Return response.choices[0].message.content on line 59, matching the Azure branch.
findings.paper_ref: README 'Setting the game and simulation configuration' (OpenAI API support)

findings.title: Constant-truthy `and` in answer/plan tag guards (benign but incorrect)
findings.claim: `if "<ANSWER>" and "</ANSWER>" in answer:` (and the identical pattern in extract_plan) always evaluates only the right operand because the non-empty string literal is truthy; the intended condition is `"<ANSWER>" in answer and "</ANSWER>" in answer`.
findings.concern: The parsing happens to stay correct because of the second `if "<ANSWER>" in answer:` fallback below it, so results are unaffected — but the guard does not do what it plainly intends and would mislead any future edit.
findings.resolution: Rewrite as `if "<ANSWER>" in answer and "</ANSWER>" in answer:` (same for the PLAN tags).

findings.title: Paper says base game is '5 parties, 6 issues'; repo base game is 6 players, 5 issues
findings.quote: Our base game adopts the setup of the initial game [44] (5 parties, 6 issues, and the values of scores and thresholds)
findings.claim: The prose attributes '5 parties, 6 issues' to the base game's setup, but games_descriptions/base/config.txt lists 6 agents and each scores_files/*.txt has 5 issue rows + 1 threshold row (6 players, 5 issues); the README/eval defaults also use AGENTS_NUM=6, ISSUES_NUM=5 for base.
findings.concern: Reader-facing dimension counts for the base game are inverted vs the shipped game; likely a description artefact (possibly describing reference [44]) rather than a result-affecting error, hence filed as a question.
findings.resolution: Please confirm the base game is 6 players / 5 issues and clarify whether '5 parties, 6 issues' refers to reference [44] rather than your base game.

findings.title: Feasible-set/random-baseline use `>=` while agent success uses strict `>` (differ ~2x)
findings.quote:
base (paper: 55 (n-1) / 12 (n) out of 720)
  '>'  (evaluate_deals / eqn4): n-1-way=37  n-way=6  total=720
  '>=' (adjust_games)         : n-1-way=55  n-way=12  total=720
  DIFFERS(n-1)=True  DIFFERS(n)=True
findings.claim: A party 'accepts' a deal iff its score exceeds its min threshold, but this is coded two ways: evaluate_deals.ipynb (loop_all_parties) uses strict `party_score > min` — which produced the paper's success rates (I reproduced 7-player 63.8/18.8/96.2 and temp1 68.8/6.2/96.9 with `>`) — whereas adjust_games.ipynb uses `deal_score >= min`, which produces the paper's feasible-deal counts (base 55 / 12 of 720, extended 204). With strict `>` the base feasible set is only 37 / 6.
findings.concern: The reported feasibility statistics and the random-chance baseline (55/720, used to argue 'agents' reasoning is crucial') are computed under a more lenient acceptance rule than the agents themselves are scored by; at the exact-threshold boundary the definitions differ nearly 2x for all-agree deals (12 vs 6), so Table 4's difficulty counts and the §4.7 baseline are not on the same footing as the success metrics, and neither the success metric (`>`) nor the count (`>=`) is consistent with both eqn. 4 (`>`) and the agents' own instructions ('cannot accept any deal with a score less than min', i.e. `>=`).
findings.resolution: Please pick one acceptance operator (matching eqn. 4 and the agent instruction) and recompute both the feasible-set/baseline counts and the success rates with it; report how much the headline rates and the 55/720 baseline move.
